pass_a_gloss: He brings forward: 'And nations will be blessed in him, and in him they will praise God in Jerusalem. For thus says the Lord to the men of Judah and to those dwelling in Jerusalem. He has spoken to those from the nations, and he has spoken to those from Israel, saying to those from Judah. I remember the former things said concerning Judah and those dwelling in Jerusalem, figuratively speaking. For we dwell, if God gives, in Jerusalem. Since where the treasure is, there also is the heart: if we treasure up in heaven, and we have our heart in Jerusalem above, concerning which the apostle says: 'But the Jerusalem above is free, which is our mother,' as it is written, and the following. 'Thus says the Lord to the men of Judah and to those dwelling in Jerusalem: Build for yourselves buildings, and do not sow upon thorns.' This word is especially said to the teachers, so that they may not first trust the things spoken to the listeners before doing the building in their souls. For when, having laid the hand upon the plough, they make buildings in their souls, according to the good and fertile ground of those hearing, then sowing they do not upon thorns. But if before the plough and before doing the building in the governing part of the listeners, one takes the holy seeds: the word concerning the Father, the word concerning the Son, the word concerning the Holy Spirit, the word concerning resurrection, the word concerning punishment, the word concerning rest, the word concerning law, the word concerning prophets, and simply each of the written things, and sows, he transgresses first the command 'Build for yourselves buildings,' second 'And do not sow upon thorns.' But someone of the listeners will say: I do not teach, I am not subject to this command. And you, become a farmer of yourself, and do not sow upon thorns, but make for me a building the place which God has entrusted to you of all things. Consider the place, see where thorns are, where worldly cares and deceit of riches and pleasure-seeking. And having considered the thorns in your soul, seek the rational plough, concerning which Jesus says: 'No one having put his hand to the plough and looking back is fit for the kingdom of God,' having sought it and found, having gathered from the writings the oxen the workers the pure, plough and build the land, and that you may no longer be old, make it new, having put off the old man with his deeds and having put on the new man being renewed for knowledge, you will make for yourself a building, and if you make the building, take seeds from the teachers, take seeds from the law, take from the prophets, from the evangelical writings, of his apostolic words, and having taken these seeds, sow the soul through memory and study. These things will appear to grow of themselves, but the true thing is not that they grow after their memory, but God will increase them: 'I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase.' And if anyone is able to understand the writings, this one has made a building and having made a building sowed not in thorns.
